subject: grey wolf
title: What If an Island Had Only Two Wolves Left? Isle Royale Did in 2016

scenes.text: What if a whole island had only two wolves left? Isle Royale did in 2016.
Isle Royale sits in Lake Superior, 15 miles offshore. Wolves crossed the ice in the 1940s; scientists have counted them since 1958.
For decades the island held about 22 wolves. Then inbreeding crashed it. By 2016: two, a father and daughter who were also half-siblings.
With no hunters, moose exploded: 1,300 in 2016, about 2,000 by 2019, stripping the forest.
So in 2018 and 2019 the park flew in 19 wolves. By winter 2026 there were 37, and the moose had fallen 75 percent, to 524.
A 2026 study says the new wolves are inbred too, but have an 80 percent chance of lasting 20 years. The study goes on.

description:
What if an island's wolves dwindled to two? On Isle Royale in Lake Superior, the longest-running predator-prey study on Earth (since 1958) watched inbreeding shrink the wolves to a single father-daughter pair by 2016, while moose boomed from 1,300 to about 2,000 by 2019.
In 2018-2019 the park relocated 19 wolves; by winter 2026 there were 37 wolves and the moose had dropped 75 percent to 524.
